newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Irkutskenergo applies to issue ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Irkutskenergo applies to issue ADRs.

text.p: Russian power utility Irkutskenergo said on Wednesday it had applied to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for permission to issue Level One American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

ADRs are securities which allow investors access in the U.S. to foreign shares without the complexities of settlement in the issuer's market. Level One ADRs, which have been issued by several Russian companies already, are the simplest and do not raise new capital.
Irkutskoye AO Energetiki i Elektrifikatsii said in a statement it had filed for SEC exemptions under rule 12g3-2(b) on Tuesday and that details of the timing of the ADR would be released later.
It said Irkutskenergo's financial adviser on the issue was Brunswick and that The Bank of New York would be the depositary bank.
Irkutskenergo is one of the most liquid stocks on the Russian Trading System. It was unchanged at $0.095 at 1000 GMT.
The company is 40 percent state-owned. The remaining 60 percent is roughly equally divided between Russian and foreign investors.

It has generating capacity of 12,914 MW and is one of just two regional generators in which national power company Unified Energy System (UES) does not hold a stake, according to a report on the sector issued earlier this year by MC Securities.

About a dozen Russian companies are planning issues of ADrs this year, The Bank of New York has said. No Russian company has yet issued Level Three ADRs which raise new capital and are listed on a U.S. stock exchange.
